The story relies almost entirely on exteriority—clinical observations of the setting, objects, and the physical movements of the characters—while offering very little interiority or emotional range. Although the narrator provides a brief justification for this detached perspective (having worked for eleven years preparing inventories), the lack of introspection, feeling, and emotional reaction makes the narrative feel flat and prevents it from achieving emotional flexibility, even as the events of the story become increasingly surreal and unsettling.
